acceptance.item: P4-RT-09-02: M6's Seen box gives the root lengths of the finite types B, C, F, G for every balanced board
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/content-m6-root-lengths.test.ts > M6's Seen box gives the root lengths of the finite types B, C, F, G for every balanced board
acceptance.evidence: severity blocker (no adjustment). Red: with the lesson at base, '1 failed' with message '... is stated with no restriction to the finite types; on the balanced board A2^(2) the simple root populations have form values 2, 8, on A4^(2) 2, 4, 8' (the reproducer's own red: tests 2 and 3 failed with 2, 8 and 2, 4, 8). Green: 1 passed. Cause: the length clause kept the scope of 'Exactly the balanced boards', while SPEC 2.5 gives 2 and 4 or 6 for the finite types only. It now reads 'on a board of finite type, short roots have form value 2, long ones 4 or 6, verified by computation'. Commit 4345046, typed in 095e84e. Adoption: the reproducer asserted that the counterexamples do not exist, which can never pass. As in the round 1 adoption of P3-RT-09-02, the test keeps them as observed facts and asserts the expected.

acceptance.item: P4-RT-09-05 and P4-RT-08-03 (DUPLICATE): M6 states Wildberger's B/C translation as 'verified by computation' for every rank of at least 3; the lists were compared for ranks 3 and 4 only
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/content-m6-wildberger-range.test.ts > M6 states Wildberger's B/C translation as 'verified by computation' for every rank of at least 3; the lists were compared for ranks 3 and 4 only; and the same file > m6-multiple-edges.mdx: the Seen box does not claim the computation for every rank from 3 up (the RT-08 reproducer, unchanged)
acceptance.evidence: severity major (no adjustment). Red at base: both tests failed ('expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []' for RT-08; the sentence as found for RT-09). Green: 4 passed. Cause: computation was claimed for every n while golden wildberger_lists.names holds B3, B4, C3, C4 (and D4, D5) only. Fix: Seen 5 now reads 'From rank 3 on, Wildberger's B and C are Bourbaki's C and B ([W20], section 9).', resting on his graphs. The box's provenance line now reads 'Verified by computation (B and C for n=3,4, D for n=4,5), ...'. Commit d677311.

deviations.what: Three RT-09 reproducers (lengths, wildberger-range, road-back) asserted that their counterexamples do not exist, which can never pass. Their tests keep the computations with the observed values and assert the finding's expected, and their first tests now assert that the sentence as found is absent. Two reproducers of one cause share one file. The captions script and the two RT-13 scripts became a source test and a Playwright test. The RT-13 test reads data-anatomy and data-out=caption hooks, not section classes, and adds an LO6 check. The Donnelly test gained one check. One type fix in the lengths helper.
